notes: The opening continuation says that a connected oriented contour amounts to an integer n≥2 and a torsor under Z/nZ. It gives cyclic-group, inverse-generator-pair and torsor data for a connected contour, then explicitly qualifies this by n≥3 and replaces the inverse pair with an abstract two-element set Ω mapping to G. The lower remark identifies an oriented contour, not necessarily connected, with a set carrying a Z-action; the unoriented counterpart stops after an ellipsis. No date or author page number is present; the pencil 6 is archival.

The source starts with connexe, not H’s Contour. It writes a two-stroke equality in “revient au =”, the abbreviation gpe, and singular Contour/ensemble/lequel in the lower remark. The above-line tel and the small cardinality parenthesis are insertions. The cancellation after partie reaches through d-apostrophe. The long line under the beginning of générateur is the returning g descender, not underlining. The final marks after equality are an unfinished ellipsis, not un.

The first circular superscript of G remains 0/circle, and its repeated notation uses the first candidate. The map label sigma/r, the flattened ou/au versus dash-like marks, cancelled ens/un and sinon/si on, and the lower variable u/n remain doubtful. The two rounded lobes of the u subscript match the established omega on scan006, settling that local doubt. The source writes bare G in item 2 bis; the superscript 0 is not supplied from context. Its opening parenthesis remains unmatched.

Targeted check: in a cyclic group generated by g of finite order n≥2, g=g⁻¹ exactly when g²=1, hence exactly when n=2. Thus the stated inverse-generator pair has cardinal two precisely for n≠2; replacing the pair by an abstract two-element set avoids its collapse when n=2. The ink’s doubtful abbreviation sss/ss/ssi is retained despite the mathematical equivalence.

Two qualifications are needed if the claims are read with the earlier loopless-contour definition. The doubly infinite path from scan005 requires the infinite cyclic group, which is absent from the opening n∈N, n≥2 description unless that sentence is limited to finite contours. Also an arbitrary Z-action may have fixed points: a singleton with the identity action would create a loop, disallowed by two distinct endpoints per edge. For loopless oriented contours the corresponding permutation must have no fixed points; its orbits then give cycles of length at least two or doubly infinite paths. These are notes on the claims, not supplied restrictions in the transcription.

check_events.outcome: For a generator of finite order n≥2, g=g⁻¹ iff g²=1 iff n=2. The pair therefore has cardinal 2 iff n≠2, and an abstract two-element Ω retains two labels at n=2.

check_events.type: refuted, with the refined statement's id
check_events.outcome: The unrestricted description includes the identity action on a singleton, which would require a loop under the preceding two-distinct-endpoints definition. Refined statement scan007-fixed-point-free-action: fixed-point-free permutations give loopless oriented contours, with finite orbits of length ≥2 or infinite cyclic orbits. The initial finite n description also needs a finite-contour restriction or an infinite-cyclic case.
